claims.text: Mother: early-stage syphilis in preg: a single dose of benzathine penicillin G; PCN-allergic pts may be desensitized, then treated w penicillin;
claims.quote: Pregnant patients in the early stages of syphilis receive a single dose of benzathine penicillin G (benzathine benzylpenicillin is used in some countries and in the United States if benzathine penicillin G is not available) (1). For later stages of syphilis or neurosyphilis, the appropriate regimen for nonpregnant patients should be followed (see Late latent or tertiary syphilis). Occasionally, a severe Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction occurs after such therapy, leading to spontaneous abortion. Patients allergic to penicillin may be desensitized and then treated with penicillin.

claims.text: erythromycin is inadequate for mother and fetus; tetracycline is contraindicated.
claims.quote: Erythromycin therapy is inadequate for both the mother and fetus and is not recommended. Tetracycline is contraindicated.

claims.text: Infant: CDC 2021: aqueous crystalline penicillin G IV or procaine penicillin G IM for 10 days; if ≥ 1 day is missed, repeat the whole course.
claims.quote: The 2021 Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) STI treatment guidelines recommend aqueous crystalline penicillin G IV or procaine penicillin G IM for 10 days. If ≥ 1 day of therapy is missed, the entire course must be repeated.
